correctness.rationale: Direct expansion yields \(\dot V=-2q\), and \(q+1/3\) is positive definite. Ellipse geometry gives area \(2\pi/(3\sqrt 3)\), integrated -q \(\pi/(9\sqrt 3)\), and uniform large-R sphere-graph expansions yield exactly the claimed area fraction and outward flux. \(\dot V\le2/3\) plus polynomial ODE continuation proves forward completeness; reversing symmetry proves backward completeness. Invariant probability identities follow by integrating two bounded-support Lie derivatives. An exact SymPy checker was run against the packaged script; all nonstandard calculations have a written derivation, and the claims do not infer global boundedness.

value.rationale: The primary literature explicitly identifies small outgoing holes on large spheres as a core numerical feature of this coexisting-torus/chaos flow, without rigorous geometry. The theorem completely determines the outward patch for all \(R\ge2\) and calculates precise natural area/flux coefficients, while supplying a rigorous global non-explosion and transverse-energy bound and exact compact-stationary orthogonality. The flux measures local radial transport and is distinguished from an escaping basin; the result is not a speculative attractor existence theorem or an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
